decision.explanation: The provided evidence (pmid-28787259:f01) describes a phase I/II study of single-agent crizotinib in patients with relapsed/refractory ALK-positive Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (ALCL). The study reports an objective response rate (ORR) of 90% and complete response (CR) rates of 83% and 80% for the 165 and 280 mg/m2 dose groups, respectively. These high response rates directly support the claim that ALK fusion status predicts sensitivity/response to crizotinib in ALCL. While the evidence does not provide specific molecular details of the ALK fusion (NEI for genomics) or pathological data (NEI for pathology), the clinical efficacy data is sufficient to support the predictive claim regarding sensitivity/response. The claim is supported by the observed clinical outcomes in the specified patient population.

citations.quote: In this phase I/II study, 26 patients with relapsed/refractory ALK-positive ALCL were administered crizotinib orally twice daily in 28-day cycles as a single agent for an indefinite duration. Patients with relapsed ALCL achieved an objective response rate of 90%. The overall response rates for patients with ALCL treated at doses of 165 and 280 mg/m2 were 83% and 90%, respectively. Rates of complete response were 83% and 80% for 165 and 280 mg/m2 dose groups, respectively. The most common grade 3 or 4 adverse event was decreased neutrophil count.
